interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into Japan's economic expansion into South America during the 1930s, showing Japanese efforts to secure strategic natural resources (oil shale at Lonquimay, Chile) and establish manufacturing footholds (textiles, toys, and porcelain) within free port zones in Uruguay to circumvent tariff barriers. It illuminates diplomatic and commercial intelligence dynamics, capturing how an Uruguayan diplomat attempted to enlist U.S. trade data to dissuade his own government from approving Japanese industrial concessions. Furthermore, the internal State Department correspondence reveals bureaucratic caution and ethical standards regarding third-party diplomatic requests, as well as the archival intersection of related Latin American investment files within State Department decimal filing.
overview: This file comprises State Department records relating to Japanese capital investment and commercial expansion in Latin America—specifically Chile and Uruguay—between January 1933 and December 1934. It opens with a cross-reference sheet to a 1933 Paris despatch from Ambassador Walter E. Edge regarding Japanese participation in the Lonquimay shale oil deposits in Chile, followed by internal State Department memoranda from late 1934 evaluating Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 910. That despatch reported an offer by Japanese manufacturers to establish textile, porcelain, and toy factories in a newly opened free port zone in Uruguay, along with an effort by the skeptical Uruguayan Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo to obtain U.S. commercial data on Japanese export growth to help defeat the scheme. Officials from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and the Division of Latin-American Affairs (including Maxwell M. Hamilton, Stanley K. Hornbeck, and Joseph F. McGurk) deliberated on the propriety of supplying such information, ultimately recommending that only public commercial data be provided and that any requests for confidential materials follow formal diplomatic channels through Washington or Montevideo.

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet referring to a Paris despatch on proposed Japanese investment in Chilean shale oil fields.
subfiles.from: Walter E. Edge (U.S. Ambassador to France)
subfiles.summary: This document file note cross-references Despatch No. 3296 of January 30, 1933, sent by Ambassador Walter E. Edge in France to the Department of State. The underlying despatch, classified under decimal file 825.6363/143, concerns Japanese participation in developing shale petroleum deposits at Lonquimay, Chile. The cross-reference was filed under decimal file 894.503125/1.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Paris Despatch No. 3296 on Lonquimay Petroleum

subfiles.about: A memorandum from the Division of Latin-American Affairs regarding whether to supply commercial data to the Uruguayan Chargé in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Joseph F. McGurk (Division of Latin-American Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Joseph F. McGurk of the Division of Latin-American Affairs replies to Maxwell M. Hamilton regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 910. McGurk states that he sees no objection to providing the Uruguayan Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo with public Department of Commerce data that would be furnished to anyone requesting it. However, if confidential information is sought, he recommends that the request come through the Uruguayan Legation in Washington or the U.S. Legation in Montevideo, advising against intimating that confidential material is available.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by J. F. McGurk on Information Requested by Uruguayan Chargé in Tokyo
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: An informal routing note from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Stanley K. Hornbeck requesting his opinion on the Tokyo despatch memorandum.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs refers the September 10 memorandum to division chief Stanley K. Hornbeck. Hamilton asks Hornbeck for a tentative expression of his opinion on the matter. The slip reflects the internal review process within the division prior to inter-divisional coordination.
subfiles.title: Routing Note from Hamilton to Hornbeck on Tokyo Despatch Memorandum
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: A Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing a Japanese proposal for factories in an Uruguayan free port zone and a request for U.S. trade data.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum reviews Despatch No. 910 of August 2, 1934, from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo regarding a proposal by Japanese manufacturers to build factories for porcelain, toys, and textiles in a recently inaugurated free port zone in Uruguay. The Uruguayan Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo recommended rejection of the proposal to his home government and asked the U.S. Embassy for statistics on Japanese export penetration into the United States to support his position. The drafter advises that only public information should be provided and expresses doubt regarding the ethics of the Chargé's use of data, recommending that formal requests be routed through the Uruguayan Legation in Washington.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Manufacturing Proposal in Uruguayan Free Port Zone
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton and Stanley K. Hornbeck
